entries.test: Public infrastructure disclosures showing the share of Microsoft's operational compute capacity devoted to OpenAI at publication.
entries.note: The preceding paragraph supplies the referent for “this.”
“Likely” explicitly qualifies the historical revenue estimate.

entries.test: Hyperscaler AI investment returns showing whether profitable recovery is possible without meeting all four stated conditions.
entries.note: “Maybe” qualifies reaching break-even; the asserted ceiling and necessary conditions are firm.
This reports his own inability to find a scenario, rather than firmly asserting that none exists.

entries.test: Customer-level cloud revenue and backlog disclosures, together with investment records, showing growth outside OpenAI and Anthropic and whether their spending requires hyperscaler funding.
entries.note: The surrounding discussion concerns cloud and AI business, particularly revenue backlogs.

entries.test: AI revenues and investment recovery accounts for Microsoft, Google and Amazon through May 19, 2027, showing whether each needed more than $100 billion annually to cover the stated investments.
entries.note: This asserts a necessary revenue threshold, not that the companies will achieve it.
The standalone proposition supplies no specific affordability or return threshold.

entries.test: Hyperscaler capital expenditure records and infrastructure commissioning disclosures showing total investment and the portion resulting in operational GPUs and capacity at publication.
entries.note: “I estimate” does not by itself turn a numerical assertion into probability language.
He gives conditions for success while explicitly doubting positive margins and loosely guessing the completion date.

entries.test: Anthropic subscription allowances, actual inference costs and subscription revenue showing whether permitted usage costs $8 to $13.50 per revenue dollar and whether inference is profitable.
entries.note: The “bedtime story” insult accompanies concrete financial assertions.

entries.test: Public contract terms and payment schedules for Anthropic's five named compute providers establishing its obligations over the stated four-year period.
entries.note: This tallies existing commitments, including estimated amounts, rather than predicting new contracts.

entries.test: Anthropic's reported operating expenses over the four years following publication showing whether they total at least $20 billion.
entries.note: “Fair to assume it will” expresses an expectation; the drafter's “likely” label is not in the quotation.
He judges the projections and prescribes how journalists should describe them.
The conclusion evaluates costs as “horrendous” and “terrible” without a shared threshold; the financing figures are separately factual.

entries.test: Anthropic's financial results if it reaches $100 billion in annualized revenue, alongside evidence of whether additional compute reduces either company's service costs.
entries.note: The preceding hypothetical supplies the revenue condition; the passage also asserts a cost mechanism.

entries.test: Public accelerator performance and cost results showing whether new silicon reduces service costs, together with Anthropic's inference revenue and cost disclosures.
entries.note: This combines an undated technology forecast with a currently checkable profitability assertion.
The central claim attributes private knowledge and an IPO-avoidance motive to the CFOs.
A “true stress-test” of AI's “true value” supplies no shared criterion for success or failure.

entries.test: Enterprise token spending, renewal and budget records alongside lab revenue and cost accounts showing whether the spending-driven revenue can be maintained economically.
entries.note: The surrounding examples give “unsustainable” a plain financial reading.

entries.test: Published enterprise AI budgets, spending forecasts, actual quarterly costs and usage policies showing whether unpredictable experimentation causes rapid budget exhaustion.
entries.note: The universal wording makes reliable forecasting and nonexperimental spending relevant counterevidence.
The compound proposition expressly includes severe doubt about the revenue figure, rather than a firm denial.
“Token binge” has no agreed boundary distinguishing it from ordinary rapid adoption or spending growth.

entries.test: Customer contracts, renewal commitments, retention data and recurring token revenue showing whether current spending represents durable revenue.
entries.note: This assesses the reliability of the existing revenue base rather than naming a future collapse date.
“Might be because” explicitly proposes only a possible explanation.
“Perfect setup” for “something dastardly” does not specify a testable act or outcome. He expressly disclaims an accusation against Anthropic.
The conditional conclusion dismisses the worth of budgets without specifying a measurable failure criterion.

entries.test: Public financial disclosures and investment records establishing whether the generative AI industry had consumed $1 trillion by publication.
entries.note: The trillion-dollar assertion is checkable; “one of the most-wasteful products” is an accompanying value judgment.
In context this is a polemical characterization, without a specified deceptive representation or transaction.

entries.test: Anthropic's subscription and enterprise revenue and cost disclosures showing whether both offerings lose money.
entries.note: The financial assertion is checkable despite the surrounding disparagement of output quality.
